facts.fact_text: The applicants are members and sympathisers of an extra-parliamentary opposition party called 'Casa noastră - Moldova' (Our home – Moldova).
The applicants participated in the large anti-government rally held on 6 September 2015 in the central square of Chișinău.
Immediately after the rally, a large group of persons led by the applicants marched towards the headquarters of the Prosecutor General's Office to demand the Prosecutor General's resignation.

The group of approximately 15-20 demonstrators, including the applicants, announced at approximately 2.18 p.m. that they intended to install tents and stay at the Prosecutor General's Office until the resignation of the Prosecutor General.
At 2.27 p.m. on 6 September 2015, several demonstrators started installing tents on the pavement in front of the Prosecutor General's Office building.
A group of demonstrators including some of the applicants were seen seated on the lower part of the steps of the Prosecutor General's Office building.
Several police officers immediately lifted the fifth applicant up and pushed him away from the entrance of the Prosecutor General's Office building.

Within two to three minutes, the demonstrators were pushed away from the entrance doors of the Prosecutor General's Office building towards the lower part of the steps by a group of policemen who outnumbered them.
At 2.29 p.m. on 6 September 2015, the police forces started pushing the demonstrators further away from the entrance of the Prosecutor General's Office building.
At 4.42 p.m. on 6 September 2015, members of the special forces and the police started taking away the tents from the pavement in front of the Prosecutor General's Office building.
In spite of some protesters' attempts to retain the tents, within two minutes all tents were taken away by the police from the pavement in front of the Prosecutor General's Office building.
At 4.47 p.m. on 6 September 2015, all the demonstrators were pushed away from both the steps, the pavement and the lawn in front of the Prosecutor General's Office building.
All the applicants were arrested at approximately 4.39 p.m. on 6 September 2015.
All the applicants were taken to a police station following their arrest on 6 September 2015.

The applicants were placed in detention for a period of seventy-two hours on suspicion of having committed the offence of participating in mass disorders provided for by Article 285 of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Moldova.
On 8 September 2015, the applicants were formally charged with the offence of participating in mass disorders under Article 285 of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Moldova.

On 26 April 2016, the court ordered as one of many surety measures in respect of the applicants other than the fourth applicant the prohibition on participating in public gatherings, if there was a risk of the gathering degenerating into mass disorders.
The prohibition on participating in public gatherings imposed on 26 April 2016 was prolonged on many occasions by the Rîşcani District Court.

Article 285(1) of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Moldova, entitled 'Mass disorders', as in force at the material time, provided that organizing or leading mass disorders involving violence against persons, pogroms, arson, damage to goods, the use of firearms or other objects used as weapons, and violent or armed resistance to representatives of authorities shall be punished by imprisonment for 4 to 8 years.

Article 285(2) of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Moldova, entitled 'Mass disorders', as in force at the material time, provided that active participation in the commission of actions set forth in Article 285(1) shall be punished by imprisonment for 3 to 7 years.

Article 285(3) of the Criminal Code of the Republic of Moldova, entitled 'Mass disorders', as in force at the material time, provided that calls for active, violent insubordination to the legitimate requests of the authorities' representatives, and for participation in mass disorders and for the commission of acts of violence against persons shall be punished by a fine in the amount of 200 to 500 conventional units or by community service for 180 to 240 hours or by imprisonment for up to 2 years.

Article 40 of the Constitution of the Republic of Moldova (on freedom of assembly) provides that all meetings, demonstrations, rallies, processions or any other assemblies are free, but they may be organised and take place only peacefully and without the use of weapons.
No violence is seen on the video footage apart from the pushing of the demonstrators by the police officers away from the entrance of the Prosecutor General's Office building.
The majority of the demonstrators stayed on the pavement, the lawn and the road in front of the Prosecutor General's Office building, with only several dozen being on the lower part of the steps.

After being pushed to the lower part of the stairs, at approximately 2.18 p.m. on 6 September 2015, a group of approximately 15-20 demonstrators, including the applicants, sat on the steps at the feet of the police cordon.
The police officers, present in great numbers, formed a line in front of the demonstrators preventing them from climbing the steps toward the entrance of the Prosecutor General's Office building.

The first applicant shouted through a megaphone that the demonstration at the Prosecutor General's Office was a peaceful demonstration and that they had the constitutional right to peacefully protest.
Judge S.B. stated in her dissenting opinion that she saw a peaceful gathering of persons protesting against the Government and expressing their discontent with the policy of the Government.
Judge S.B. stated in her dissenting opinion that the demonstration of 6 September 2015 had taken place on a Sunday and had not hindered in any way the work of the Prosecutor General's Office.
